neighbours.label: A point inside a description of how a scene or object looks (peaks rising majestically, stairways reaching to the sky, glossy finishes, a pool truly sapphire blue), vs narrative or administrative sentences about the same places and products
fire: Below the cliffs, the bay glitters turquoise, ringed by white sand and dark pines.
The cathedral's spires soar upward, lacy and pale against the evening sky.
The phone comes in three finishes: matte black, silver and rose gold.
Rows of vineyards roll away toward distant hills wrapped in blue haze.
The lake is perfectly still, reflecting the snowy peaks like a mirror.
Lanterns hang from every eave, glowing red and gold over the narrow lane.
The waterfall plunges in a long white ribbon into a deep green pool.
The dunes stretch to the horizon, rippled and copper in the late sun.
quiet: The bay was closed to fishing boats for two weeks in March.
The cathedral's board voted to raise the entrance fee next year.
The phone ships with a charger and a one-year warranty.
The vineyard hired twelve new workers for the harvest season.
The lake association meets on the first Monday of every month.
The lane was repaved last year after residents complained.
Tickets for the waterfall tour can be bought at the visitor center.
The dune permit costs twenty dollars and must be renewed annually.

predictions: Visual descriptions reach 0.5-1.0; non-visual sentences about the same places or products stay under 0.1.
